requirements.note: Newest first, grouped by day under inset-grouped cards; each header reads 'Oct 25, 2026 · $222.02' (date and day total on one line).
'THIS MONTH $5,269.70 · October 2026 · 86 expenses' card at the top; it updates on add, edit and delete.

Sheet with amount on the decimal pad, merchant, a 7-category pop-up menu, a date picker defaulting to today and an optional note. Save (a checkmark) stays disabled until the amount is greater than zero, with inline helper text. The new row appears under a new 'Oct 27' group.
Tapping a row opens an 'Edit Expense' sheet filled in from the row; changes save. A trailing swipe shows a red Delete action that removes the row and updates the totals.
Categories tab is sorted largest first, with amount, count, '% of total' and a progress bar. Tapping a category pushes a list of its month's transactions grouped by day, with a summary.
Amounts are formatted as $#,###.##. Added, edited and deleted rows all survived relaunch.

bugs: At the largest text size the Categories rows break words and numbers letter by letter ('Bill' / 's', '1' / '6' / 'e' / 'x' stacked vertically) because the name and amount stay side by side in a fixed row.
tells: Categories at the largest text size: the category name and expense count wrap one character per line instead of the row switching to a stacked layout.
Mid-swipe, the row's merchant and subtitle disappear and the row turns into a grey slab with only the amount showing, which is not how a system swipe action looks.
Category rows and expense rows have no icons or colour; the result is plain and functional, but generic.
The category drill-down uses a small inline title, while the other screens use large titles.
Main-list headers join date and total in one string ('Oct 25, 2026 · $222.02') instead of putting the total on the trailing side.
The form's 'Expense' section header and the merchant field without a label are slightly unusual; the 'Enter an amount greater than zero.' footer shows before the user has typed anything.
A.scroll: Smooth native collection-view scrolling: slow drags and flings showed no blank rows or pop-in, rubber-banding at the top works, and scroll position is kept when switching tabs.

requirements.note: Newest first, grouped by day. Headers read 'Sun, Oct 25' with the day total trailing, and a new item's day is labelled 'Today'. Rows have tinted category icons.
Summary card shows 'OCTOBER 2026 · This month's spending $5,269.70' with a segmented category colour bar and the expense count; it updates live.

Sheet with a large '$ 0.00' amount field on the decimal pad, merchant, a pushed category picker with icons and a checkmark, a date defaulting to today and an optional note. Save with an empty or zero amount shows red inline errors ('Enter an amount greater than $0…', 'Enter a merchant name.') and does not save.
Tapping a row opens 'Edit expense' filled in from the row; edits save. A trailing swipe shows a red Delete action, which deletes and updates the totals.

Categories tab: a 'Monthly breakdown' sorted largest first, with icon, amount, '% of spending', a coloured bar and a chevron. Tapping one pushes a large-title screen (e.g. 'Shopping') with that category's month total and its transactions grouped by day.
US currency formatting throughout. An added expense, its edit, and its deletion all persisted across relaunch.

tells: A custom purple accent, a filled purple Save capsule and a tinted summary card give it a branded look rather than stock iOS. Well executed, but not system-default.
The tab is named 'Activity' while the screen's title is 'Expenses'.
Lowercase sheet titles ('New expense', 'Edit expense') where iOS convention is title case.
Validation errors appear only after Save is tapped, rather than Save being disabled until the form is valid.
B.scroll: Smooth native table scrolling: slow drags and repeated flings showed no blank rows, jumps or pop-in, the top rubber-bands normally, and position is kept across tab switches.

why: Both apps meet every requirement, scroll natively and persist correctly. B is more polished: category icons and colours, a category picker with icons, clear inline validation, large titles on the drill-down, and a layout that reflows cleanly at the largest text size. A's Categories screen breaks words letter by letter at the largest size, and its swipe-to-delete row looks odd mid-swipe.
